targetAudience.primary: Architects of agent platforms, MCP runtimes and permission systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands runtime sessions, capability attachment and authorization refresh.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A broad mutable permission object lets one runtime refresh overwrite authority belonging to another attachment.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change publishes explicit per-server MCP permission profiles and refuses call preparation when attachment authority cannot be resolved.

externalHook.description: Sharing a server identity does not imply sharing the mutable authority that governs its tools.

coreProposition: Permission authority should follow the attachment/runtime lifecycle it governs: resolve and publish authority per server, reject unresolved authority, and let refresh replace only the owning scope rather than a broad shared manager.

originalValue.description: Separates resource discovery from authority ownership and treats refresh as a versioned scoped transition rather than global configuration replacement.

readerTakeaway: Give every permission snapshot an owner, lifecycle and replacement boundary; fail closed when ownership is unresolved and audit which scope a refresh changes.

supported: Enabled MCP servers receive explicit published permission profiles.
Unresolved server authority prevents MCP call preparation.
Approval, elicitation and sandbox-sensitive paths consume server-specific authority across demonstrated refresh paths.
uncertain: The right scope for future threadless MCP operations

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article establishes a general authority-ownership pattern without a first-party project.

decisionReason: The per-server profile map, preparation guard and downstream consumers support a bounded attachment-authority argument.
